purpose: Theophylline is used to help open up the airways in your lungs, making it easier to breathe. It is commonly prescribed for conditions like asthma, chronic bronchitis, and COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease). It helps reduce wheezing, shortness of breath, and chest tightness.
how_it_works: Theophylline works by relaxing the muscles around your airways, allowing them to open up wider so air can flow in and out more easily. It also helps reduce inflammation in the lungs and stimulates your breathing muscles to work more effectively. Think of it like loosening a tight belt around your airways so you can breathe more freely.
common_side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, stomach upset, headache, feeling restless or jittery, trouble sleeping, increased urination, and a faster or irregular heartbeat. These are more likely if the level of medication in your blood gets too high.
warnings: This medication requires regular blood tests to make sure the level in your blood stays in the safe range — too much can be dangerous and cause seizures or serious heart problems. Many common medications, foods like caffeine, and even smoking can change how this drug works in your body, so always tell your doctor and pharmacist about everything you take. Do not stop or change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: Dosing is very individual and depends on your age, weight, health conditions, and other medications. Adults typically start at a low dose taken once or twice daily, and your doctor will slowly adjust it based on blood tests. Always take it exactly as prescribed and try to take it at the same time each day.
